HARDWARE / ELECTRONICS PROJECT

Dark Detector Circuit

An automatic lighting circuit designed to detect low-light conditions using an LDR and activate an LED through an NPN transistor.

Electronics LDR NPN Transistor Circuit Design Breadboard
01 / OVERVIEW

Project Overview

What is it?

A Dark Detector is an electronic device that senses the absence of light or low-light conditions. When darkness is detected, the circuit automatically activates an output such as an LED or lamp.

Project Goal

The goal of this project was to build a simple automatic light-control circuit that reacts to changes in ambient light without requiring manual switching.

LDR Sensor
NPN Transistor

02 / VISUALS

Circuit Design & Implementation

Circuit diagram showing the LDR, NPN transistor, LED, resistors and 9V power supply.

03 / WORKING PRINCIPLE

How It Works

01

The LDR senses the surrounding light.

The resistance of the Light Dependent Resistor changes according to the amount of light reaching it.

02

In bright light, the circuit stays OFF.

When there is enough light, the detector does not activate the LED.

03

In darkness, the LDR resistance increases.

The change in resistance affects the transistor's control signal.

04

The transistor activates the LED.

When darkness is detected, the transistor allows the LED to turn ON automatically.

Simple idea: Less light → darkness detected → LED turns ON automatically.
04 / APPLICATIONS

Where It Can Be Used

Streetlights
